title: ML models first-class concept: underdeveloped; no stdlib support or examples; stdlib ML does not use model interface
description:
## Summary

Tactus treats ML models as a first-class concept (DSL model "name" { ... }, ModelPrimitive, ModelBackend with predict / predict_sync, checkpointing). That idea is not well-developed: there is no standard library support or code examples that use it, and existing stdlib ML features do not conform to this interface.

## Evidence

- **Stdlib:** tactus/stdlib/tac/tactus/classify/llm.tac implements LLMClassifier by composing an Agent (conversational LLM), not by using the model primitive or any ModelBackend. So "ML" in the stdlib is agent-based and does not go through the standard model interface.
- **Stdlib README:** tactus/stdlib/README.md lists tactus.classify (LLM + fuzzy) and does not mention the model primitive or any stdlib modules that use it.
- **Examples:** examples/models/ contains a README with brief model(...) snippets and a Python script for creating a sentiment model; there are no full .tac examples that demonstrate the model primitive end-to-end in a procedure.

## Desired direction (for later work)

Align stdlib and examples with the first-class model concept: add stdlib support and examples that use model "..." { ... } and the ModelBackend contract, and/or refactor stdlib classifiers (e.g. LLMClassifier) to use the model interface where appropriate so that all ML inference is consistent and checkpointed.
creator: Ryan Alyn Porter

custom.beads_close_reason: Stdlib and examples now use Model primitive; LLMClassifier delegates to Model; stdlib README updated
